## Implementation Report — round 7 (crash-fix round 4: attempt-4 p3_ladder OOM)

**Status:** READY-FOR-REVIEW

### Diagnosis (live-pod forensics, pod-1333)

Class **(a)** — leftover engine residue, NOT (b) scheduler double-mapping, NOT (c) unit arithmetic:

- The p3 scheduler serialized GPU 0 correctly: main log shows `basepriors all` -> gpu 0 at 15:56:07, slot freed, `ladder ext_icl` -> gpu 0 at 15:57:17. No double-mapping (so no scheduler-mapping fix/test; the brief's (b) branch is ruled out by the fanout log).
- The ladder unit's own arithmetic fits a clean 80 GB GPU: engine 41.25 GiB (util 0.5) + HF base ~15.3 GiB + ctx ≈ 57.5 < 79.18. No util downsizing needed.
- The killer: **29.09 GiB of p0/p1-era vLLM EngineCore residue (host pid 1213661)**. The in-process `[teardown]` scan first flagged it at **15:29:52 during p1_mixes** and on every subsequent teardown (15:30:26 / 15:30:59 / 15:31:30 / 15:32:01 / 15:56:59) — it survived ~28 min through ALL of p2 (LoRA fanout + ZeRO-3 FT) into p3, where 29.09 + 41.25 + HF load left 81 MiB free at the OOM. Key mechanism: this pod's container has its OWN pid namespace (self-reported EngineCore pids 27916/30285 vs NVML pids ~1.2M), so NVML pids are HOST-namespace — `/proc/<pid>` never exists in-container, the existing `_log_zombie_cuda_contexts` misreads every live holder as an unkillable "dead pid" and only WARNs, and `_reap_vllm_engine`'s getattr-guarded `engine_core.shutdown()` had no verification that the child actually died. A ~28-min-stable 29 GiB allocation is a LIVE orphan (driver releases dead-process accounting in seconds), consistent with an EngineCore whose graceful shutdown didn't take; it cleared only when the dispatcher died at 15:58 (GPUs read 0 MiB at diagnosis time).

### (a) What was done

- `scripts/issue1333_dispatch.py` (+509/-14 net across 2 commits):
  - **Root cause — `_reap_engine` hardened:** composes `_reap_vllm_engine` (graceful v1 shutdown + destroy_process_group) with a DETERMINISTIC psutil child sweep by CONTAINER pid (`_is_engine_child`: enginecore/vllm/multiprocessing.spawn; wandb-protected per #1090) + gc/empty_cache/ipc_collect + 1s async-release sleep. Logs `[engine-reap] engine children reaped (n=K)`. Deliberately NO foreign-pid drain verdict at this seam (see (b)).
  - **Hygiene layer 1 — phase boundaries:** `_gpu_hygiene(label)` at `_fanout_units` entry + exit (every fanout phase: p2 train, p3 ladder/basepriors, p4-p7) and before the whole-pod ZeRO-3 FT launch (`p2_train:pre-ft`). It (1) empty_caches its OWN allocator first (the main dispatcher caches ~15 GiB after in-process p0/p1 HF reads — cached blocks surface under an unattributable host pid), (2) reaps surviving engine-child stragglers by container pid, (3) bounded drain-wait (`_wait_gpus_free`, floor 2048 MiB, timeout 180 s, env-overridable `EPM_GPU_HYGIENE_{FLOOR_MIB,TIMEOUT_S}`) — fail LOUD with the raw nvidia-smi dump + host-namespace caveat when a live holder never drains.
  - **Hygiene layer 2 — per-unit preflight:** `_unit_gpu_preflight(kind, gpu_id)` in `main()`'s unit branch, BEFORE any engine/model load: the CVD-pinned GPU (fallback `--gpu-id`) must drain below 2048 MiB within 180 s (`EPM_UNIT_PREFLIGHT_*`), else RuntimeError with the dump — a fast named failure instead of attempt-4's 41-GiB-deep OOM. Emits `[unit-preflight] gpu=<k> free`. This also protects fanout slot REUSE (the exact ext_icl-after-basepriors handoff).
  - **Unit-END group reap:** `_reap_completed_unit_group(proc, extra)` on EVERY unit exit (clean or failed) in `_fanout_units` — an orphaned EngineCore reparents to init (invisible to psutil from the dispatcher) but keeps the unit's pgid (`start_new_session=True`), so killpg is the only container-side handle; no-op (ProcessLookupError) in the healthy case.
  - Pure, injectable probe helpers for CPU-testability: `_smi_query`, `_per_gpu_used_mib` (reuses `eval_battery._parse_compute_app_rows`, `[N/A]` = unknown = above-floor), `_wait_gpus_free(smi=, sleep=)`.

phase: p3_ladder engine/HF teardown seams (issue1333_dispatch.py)
lesson: A free-helper that does `del model; gc.collect(); torch.cuda.empty_cache()` frees NOTHING while the caller still binds the object — `del` drops only the callee's parameter binding, and empty_cache releases only unreferenced blocks. Any floor-gated VRAM drain-wait placed after such a "free" deterministically times out on the caller's resident weights. Fix shape: take-and-return-None helper with call-site rebinding (`x = _free_hf(x)`), drop wrapper objects that pin the base (PeftModel holds its base model even after `.unload()`), then gc+empty_cache AFTER the last rebind so nvidia-smi-visible memory actually returns to the driver.
